title: GTN-Cell: Efficient Standard Cell Characterization Using Graph Transformer Network
problem: Traditional lookup-table (LUT) based NLDM (nonlinear delay model) becomes inaccurate at advanced nodes; Current Source Model (CSM) is more accurate but requires extensive SPICE simulations, creating bottleneck in standard cell library design.
motivation: Technology scaling demands more accurate cell characterization; CSM provides better accuracy but manual transistor-level simulation is prohibitively expensive.
method: Graph Transformer Network (GTN) learns transistor-level cell structures as graphs. Transformer encoder captures global node relationships via path-related positional encodings. GTN predicts CSM waveforms directly from circuit topology, reducing SPICE simulations by 70% while maintaining accuracy.
key_novelty: Graph representation of transistor circuits combined with transformer architecture (positional encodings for circuit paths) to enable end-to-end CSM waveform prediction from topology.
contributions: 2.27% average error on predicted voltage waveforms across standard cells and timing arcs
Generalizable to different standard cell types and timing arcs
limitations: Evaluation limited to specific cell library; generalization to other process nodes and extreme corner conditions not addressed.
primary_theme: graph transformer for CSM waveform prediction in cell characterization
